title: Deconfounding Game 2: smoking across two pregnancies
content: First-pregnancy smoking and stable physiological causes meet at a latent abnormality. Prior miscarriage descends from that collider, so adjusting for it opens a back-door path between current smoking and future miscarriage unless either side of the path is also blocked.

variables.name: Prior Abnormality (B)
variables.content: An unobservable abnormality in the first pregnancy.

variables.name: Prior Miscarriage (C)
variables.content: Observed miscarriage history, descended from B.

variables.name: Other Physiological Causes (D)
variables.content: Stable physiological causes shared across pregnancies.

variables.name: Current Smoking (X)
variables.content: Smoking at the beginning of the second pregnancy.

variables.name: Current Abnormality (E)
variables.content: An unobservable abnormality in the second pregnancy.

variables.name: Future Miscarriage (Y)
variables.content: Miscarriage outcome in the second pregnancy.

arrows.because: First-pregnancy smoking can induce the first abnormality.
The first abnormality can cause the observed prior miscarriage.
Smoking behavior can persist or change between pregnancies.
Other stable physiological causes can induce the first abnormality.
The same physiological causes can induce the second abnormality.
Current smoking can induce the second abnormality.
The second abnormality can cause future miscarriage.
